clue.text: Language learner I included in description of top class

indicators.note: things included in something else sit inside it, so these letters go into the next word

parts.note: posh describes the upper class
L is the learner plate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student of languages joins an exclusive top-set class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language learner' reads as one phrase, but 'Language' is the definition and the learner is just the L-plate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is the national tongue of Poland, a West Slavic language.

clue.text: The old man's attempt to make some dough

parts.note: pa is a father, the old man, and 's is kept
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Dad has a go at earning some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like slang for money, but here it is the baker's dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is a stiff dough of flour, fat and water, so it is one kind of dough.

clue.text: Silly male term of endearment for people on the way out

indicators.note: silly means foolish, so the letters that follow are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
ducks is a northern English affectionate address, like love or dear

explanation.surface: A man's daft pet name for colleagues about to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' reads as describing the man, but it mixes the letters of 'male'. Ducks is a friendly British form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: Lame ducks are officials serving out their time before a successor takes over, so they are on the way out.

clue.text: Support from university after second shameful mark

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
U is the abbreviation for university
a stain is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A university withdraws its backing after a second disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places U behind S; STAIN then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to bear the weight of, so it is a synonym of the verb support.

clue.text: Cross Tories oddly admitting claims

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the other word goes inside
oddly means taking the letters in odd positions only, first, third and fifth

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word
to aver is to assert or claim

explanation.surface: Angry Conservatives, behaving strangely, let in some assertions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective for angry Tories, but it is the verb meaning to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something, so it is a synonym of the verb cross.

clue.text: Averted changes around start of work in theatre — began operating again

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround the next piece
changes means the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Act I is the opening section of a stage play

explanation.surface: A disaster averted, a theatre's opening production got going again.
explanation.walkthrough: Act I, the first act of a play, is the start of a theatrical work; it sits after the first two letters of the mixed AVERTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactivated means switched on or brought into action once more after a pause.

clue.text: Meat cooked in ovens — does provide some of it

definitions.text: Meat cooked in ovens — does provide some of it

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the following letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Roast meat, some of it supplied by female deer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it: does are female deer, and their flesh is the meat roasted in ovens.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the flesh of deer eaten as food, and does are female deer, so they supply it.

clue.text: Take part in administration nine to five, say

indicators.note: taking part of a word means lifting a stretch of letters out of it

parts.note: five letters from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: An office worker joins the admin staff on standard working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine to five' looks like office hours; read as numbers it is a proportion, 9:5.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine to five, written 9:5, is an example of a numerical proportion between two quantities.

clue.text: Thrilling performer's going off about clubs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the departure word wraps the other

parts.note: an actor's leaving the stage is exiting
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A dazzling act ends with the performer walking off the stage swinging clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performer's' is 'performer is', the actor's exit from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting means causing great enthusiasm and eagerness, a synonym of thrilling.

clue.text: Asian food son found in Polynesian islands

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Samoa is an island group in Polynesia
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A traveller's son discovers South Asian snacks while in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside SAMOA after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry with a spiced filling, a staple of South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Acting with me could be so attractive

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor boasts that performing alongside them would be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting' reads as stage work but is simply letters to mix with ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic means drawing things toward it, and figuratively a person who draws others in is attractive.

clue.text: Covering for those who have arrived and are arriving

definitions.text: Covering for those who have arrived and are arriving

parts.words: Covering for those who have arrived
parts.note: surface reading: some shelter or insurance for people who have just turned up

parts.words: those who have arrived and are arriving
parts.note: setter's reading: celebrities who have 'arrived' in life, walking into a premiere on a ceremonial floor covering

explanation.surface: Something provided to shelter guests both already present and still coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrived' carries its second sense of having become famous; the covering is on the ground, rolled out for stars as they turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: This ceremonial floor runner is laid down for VIPs at premieres and state visits, so it literally covers the ground for celebrities as they enter.

clue.text: I proceed farcically, swallowing pie in costume drama, perhaps

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the mixed letters enclose the next word
doing something farcically is doing it in a ridiculous muddle, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor carries on absurdly, eating a pie in the middle of a historical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A period piece is a work set in a past era, and a costume drama is a typical example.

clue.text: Rum, initially, in one small drink or another

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the next word

parts.note: a shot is a single small measure of spirits

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Asking for rum first, someone settles for one small drink or some other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another kind of small drink: a short is a measure of spirits, as opposed to a long drink like beer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs a short is a small serving of spirits, so it is another small drink alongside a shot.

clue.text: Breach agreement about returning paintings

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the agreement word wraps round the other

parts.note: a convention is a formal agreement, as between states

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so that word is read backwards

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a deal over the return of borrowed paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: A contravention is an infringement of a rule or law, so it is a breach.

clue.text: Isn't seen moving around without resistance — due to this?

definitions.text: Isn't seen moving around without resistance — due to this?

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters surround the next piece
moving the letters around means putting them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Something not seen moving, even without resistance, must owe its stillness to this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it: a body at rest stays at rest with nothing pushing on it, through inertia.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertness is the state of not moving or acting, the reason a thing is seen to stay still.

clue.text: Great shot

parts.note: surface reading: praise for an excellent strike or photograph
setter's reading: a great person who has been shot, as on camera for the cinema

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a noun phrase, a 'great' is a famous person and 'shot' means filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen celebrity is a famous person who is filmed, so a great who has been shot by a movie camera.

clue.text: At home game, holding up — showing skill beyond defence?

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the game word grips the next one

parts.note: a sport is a game
taken as written
able means skilful

explanation.surface: A home match where a team holds firm, showing skill that defenders cannot cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond defence' reads as football, but means unable to be defended or justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Insupportable means unjustifiable or indefensible, so it describes something that cannot be defended.

clue.text: Finish off soup and second dish

indicators.note: to finish off is to deal with the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word
the latter is the second of two

explanation.surface: Eat up the soup, then the next course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' sounds like eating up the soup but takes only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large flat serving dish.

clue.text: Continuously attack doctor in committee

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a board is a governing committee
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A medic sitting on a committee is relentlessly harangued.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard is to attack persistently, originally with artillery, so it means attack without let-up.

clue.text: French language in British college

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British
Eton College is the English public school

explanation.surface: French is on the timetable at a British school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' joins definition and wordplay; Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton is the Celtic language spoken in Brittany, so a language of France.

clue.text: Male assistant put back channels of communication

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the helper word is read from the end

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A male helper is demoted, and the press and broadcasters hear of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the means of mass communication: press, radio, television and online outlets.

clue.text: Impressionist past his prime sent up head of state

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: aged means old, past one's best

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stage mimic, now over the hill, mocks the leader of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' and 'sent up' suggest a comic mimic; it is the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French painter of the Impressionist movement, famous for his ballet dancers.

clue.text: House member outside party encountered recorder of steps taken

indicators.note: outside means lying around the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords
a do is a party
met means encountered

explanation.surface: An MP or lord bumped into someone outside a party, and a note was kept of their movements.
explanation.walkthrough: The House here is the House of Lords, the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, whose members are lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer is a small device that counts the walker's paces, so it records steps taken.

clue.text: From Toronto, get here at the same time

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the run starts at the end of the city name and ends at the last word

explanation.surface: An instruction to travel here from Toronto, all arriving at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Together means simultaneously, as when things happen together at one moment.

clue.text: Keen to secure a mile in fast time

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so the fast word encloses the others

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: An eager runner hopes to clock a fast mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' and 'fast' both read as athletics; keen is the verb meaning to wail, and fast means abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief for the dead, which is to lament.

clue.text: Private was in the army again?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kept for someone, or reticent and keeping to oneself
second meaning: served a second time in the forces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an army rank to go with the second half, but it is the adjective; the question mark flags the split reading of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved keeps their feelings private, and the word can be split to mean served again in the military.

clue.text: Remaining child very likely to succeed

parts.note: an odd one is the one left over
a son is a child

explanation.surface: The surviving child is tipped to inherit everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' suggests inheriting, but it is the betting sense of winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on is a betting term for a runner whose chance of winning is better than even, hence highly probable.
